attributes.residual: TWO named mechanisms, both non-source-reachable. (1) ENTRY-SCHEDULE WINDOW @0x134-0x168, 6 rows, multiset IDENTICAL: target hoists the u32->f64 bias literal (lfd @0x138) ahead of the gCurLevel load (@0x144) and recycles f1 for the later `lfs ene_speed`; ours hoists the gCurLevel load to @0x134 and sinks the bias lfd to @0x154, so ene_speed needs a second FPR (f2). This is precisely the shape claim.law.repeated-fp-pool-literal-first-load-is-position-invariant.20260831.v1 declares source-unreachable (the pool constant's first materialization position is chosen by the allocate-then-schedule pipeline, not by statement position); that law also explicitly forbids the extern-literal sweep here. (2) CLOSED 2-CYCLE CALLEE-SAVED TRANSPOSITION over the whole function: r29<->r30 (shown vs the lbl_80344740 visibility counter) and f25<->f26 (the lfs lbl_80346980 / lfd lbl_80346928 pair). Both webs have identical live ranges and identical spill weight in the two streams - a genuine allocator tie. NOT WEBFRANK-ELIGIBLE: mechanism (1) is a schedule difference, so this is a permutation+schedule COUPLED residual, which claim.law.webfrank-permutation-is-audited-in-our-colouring.20260831.v1 and the WF2 lane's sysResetService precedent both exclude from the pure-recolor path. Save set is EXACT in both streams (_savefpr_25 + stmw r28,64(r1), frame 136), so the invisible-blocker class is ruled out.
